extraction.name: Vibravox
extraction.description: A GDPR-compliant French speech dataset with audio recordings from five body-conduction audio sensors and one airborne reference microphone, including speech samples, physiological sounds, recording-condition annotations, and linguistic transcriptions collected from 188 participants under quiet and noisy acoustic conditions.
extraction.creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poiree, Veronique Zimpfer, Eric Bavu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data were collected from participants wearing six simultaneously recorded sensors in a controlled setup. Each participant completed four consecutive recording phases: reading French Wikipedia sentences in quiet conditions, remaining silent in spatialized noise, remaining silent in quiet conditions, and reading in noisy conditions. Recordings were made with a 56-loudspeaker 3D spatializer for noisy subsets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Direct measurement, Experiments, Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some collected recordings were excluded due to mispronunciations, sensor shifts, sensor malfunctions, or missing microphones; 188 of 200 participants and 28,471 of 30,568 sentences were retained after filtering.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data include six-channel audio recordings from five body-conduction sensors and one airborne headset microphone, participant-read French Wikipedia/Common Voice text, AudioSet noise samples, and in-house ambisonic recordings of concerts and street events.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For noisy-condition modeling, the authors dynamically or statically mixed speech-clean recordings with speechless-noisy recordings to simulate noisy speech while preserving a clean reference.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing included applying a 20 Hz high-pass filter to each acquisition channel; filtering and normalizing text by removing proper names, numbers, Greek letters, mathematical symbols, and syntactic errors; lowercasing and removing punctuation except apostrophes; generating phonetic transcriptions; and post-processing audio with automatic filters based on phoneme error rate, SNR, and sensor drift. Voice activity timestamps were extended by 0.6 seconds and trimmed by 15 ms when needed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations include recording-condition metadata and linguistic transcriptions. Text was normalized and converted to IPA phonetic transcriptions using the CoML lab phonemizer, with manual phonetic transcription for unrecognized words.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality was analyzed using phoneme error rate between labeled phonetic transcriptions and Whisper-derived phonetic transcriptions; samples with PER greater than 10% were discarded to ensure high-quality labels.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: CoML lab text phonemizer; whisper-timestamped model based on Whisper
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender/sex, voice recordings, physiological sounds, and biometric information related to identity, heart rate, and breathing.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to support robust communication systems and applications such as military and industrial communication, access control, intelligence gathering, voice commands, and monitoring vital signs.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes deliberate recruitment of a diverse and gender-balanced participant group to improve representativeness and inclusivity.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to French, and some sensors have limited bandwidth or fitting issues. The authors note that post-processing excluded 6% of participants and 6.8% of sentences to prioritize rigorous analysis and fair microphone comparison rather than maximizing performance.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing for speech enhancement, speech-to-phonemes recognition, and speaker verification; also useful for simulating noisy scenarios, developing voice commands, monitoring vital signs, and generating synthetic datasets with realistic physiological and sensor noise.

name.evidence: Abstract —Vibravox is a dataset compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) containing audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors

description.evidence: Abstract —Vibravox is a dataset compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) containing audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors: two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone. The dataset also includes audio data from an airbome microphone used as a reference. The Vibravox corpus contains 45 hours per sensor of speech samples and physiological sounds recorded by 188 participants under different acoustic conditions imposed by a high order ambisonics 3D spatializer. Annotations about the recording conditions and linguistic transcriptions are also included in the corpus.
